title: Run agent (prompt)
text: The Svelte form trims the prompt and prevents duplicate submissions.
explanation: A synchronous lock applies before any async work. Validation is repeated on the server.

title: POST /api/agent/stream
text: The browser posts JSON to a relative same-origin endpoint.
explanation: SvelteKit serves the UI and API on the same Node server. Private configuration never enters this client.

title: Validate; tools disabled
text: The server treats all JSON input as untrusted.
explanation: The request reader also bounds actual body bytes, validates content type and checks Origin. The SDK independently disables built-in tools.

title: streamAgent() / query()
text: A real SvelteKit POST route delegates to the server-only handlers.
code: export function POST({ request }: { request: Request }) { return handlers().stream(request); }
explanation: The runtime composes validated configuration and the SDK service per request. Client modules cannot import this server-only directory.

title: Prompt; no built-in tools
text: The actual SDK query boundary owns the CLI runtime and model transport.
explanation: The application supplies a prompt and typed options, then consumes SDK messages. The model exchange itself is internal to the SDK.

title: Model response
text: Observe SDK messages until a final result appears.
explanation: This runAgent excerpt shows the same loop as the terminal lesson. streamAgent consumes the iterator while forwarding safe progress projections.

title: Safe SDK message
text: Only allowlisted data leaves the SDK service.
explanation: Text, system subtype and final metrics are projected. Thinking, tool inputs, paths, session IDs and raw configuration are excluded.

title: SSE message event
text: The handler encodes UTF-8 SSE frames.
explanation: Heartbeat comments keep the stream active. Request abort, reader cancellation and the three-minute deadline clean up execution.

title: Update typed state
text: Each safe event appends a timestamped Svelte timeline row.
explanation: The 500-row display limit does not prevent final-result processing. State belongs to this component, rather than a shared server store.

title: ResultMessage fields
text: Normalize answer, turns, duration, estimated cost and error flag.
explanation: Non-success subtypes remain failures even if is_error is false. Exact key occurrences are redacted; absent cost remains null.

title: SSE ResultMessage
text: Validate the final-result contract before delivery to Svelte.
explanation: ResultMessage is a public presentation label for a safe SDK result projection. It uses the same SSE message event as progress.

title: Render answer + metrics
text: Sanitize Markdown and highlighted code before rendering HTML.
explanation: Svelte HTML insertion receives only sanitized Markdown. CodeBlock uses escaped Highlight.js output for trusted source snippets and DOMPurify in the browser.

title: SSE done event
text: Require both a final result and done before resolving the stream.
explanation: Transport completion does not override an SDK error result. The parser handles split UTF-8, CRLF, comments and multiple frames.

title: SSE error; no done
text: A failure after SSE starts emits a safe error without done.
code:
} catch { sendEvent('error', { detail: FAILURE }); }
finally { finish(); }
explanation: Query failures instead return HTTP 502. Raw provider exceptions and submitted values never enter these error details.

title: Error + snackbar
text: Show the safe error and snackbar, then restore controls.
explanation: Specific HTTP validation and origin details survive the client boundary. Completion and teardown clear timers and cancel owned requests.

title: Key: SSE error / input: 422
text: A missing key ends the stream before the SDK service is called.
code:
if (!config.apiKeyConfigured) { sendEvent('error', { detail: MISSING_KEY }); finish(); return; }
request.signal.addEventListener('abort', abort, { once: true });
explanation: Simple mode returns 503. Invalid prompts are rejected with 422 before SSE headers. Neither path calls the model.
